strengths: Introduces a novel and well-motivated threat model (Erasure Evasion Backdoors) that unifies data-based and weight-based backdoor injection to circumvent concept erasure, filling a clear gap since prior work studied backdoors and erasure largely in isolation.

Extensive empirical evaluation spanning three tasks (celebrity/personal-rights erasure, object erasure, explicit-content erasure), six erasure methods including three that explicitly claim adversarial robustness (RECE, RECELER, AdvUnlearn), two model families/architectures (SD v1.4, SD v2.1) plus a preliminary extension to the DiT-based FLUX model, which strengthens generality claims.

The proposed EEB_deep score-based attack is a reasonably principled construction (self-distillation with trigger/quality/retention losses) and is shown via ablations (Table 8, Table 9, Fig. 10) to be necessary in its components and to have been tuned sensibly (e.g., iteration count, alpha weighting).

Goes beyond just demonstrating the attack: includes trajectory analysis across erasure iterations (Supp. C), multi-trigger and multi trigger-target experiments (Supp. E), and a defense/detectability discussion (WeightWatcher weight-deviation diagnostics, T2IShield activation monitoring) that partially mitigates the paper being purely offensive.

Good reproducibility effort: detailed supplementary material describing hyperparameters, official implementations used for baselines, prompt templates, computational cost breakdown, and a stated commitment to release code/templates and a responsible disclosure timeline for full model checkpoints.
Clear framing of ethical considerations (censored explicit content, impact statement, discussion of responsible disclosure) appropriate for a dual-use security paper.
weaknesses: The core threat model requires the adversary to have released/poisoned the model or training data before erasure is applied, and for defenders to then obtain and use that exact poisoned model unmodified; the practical likelihood and typical pipeline for this scenario (e.g., why a safety-conscious deployer would fine-tune/erase directly on an untrusted third-party checkpoint without further vetting) is not deeply justified or discussed relative to more standard backdoor threat models.

The white-box EEB_deep variant assumes an adversary with substantial control over U-Net fine-tuning (LoRA across all layers) and knowledge that the model owner will apply concept erasure afterward and not further fine-tune/train on curated data; this fairly strong and specific assumption is somewhat inconsistent with the more constrained EEB_surface/shallow variants and the differing feasibility across variants is not always foregrounded when synthesizing headline numbers in the abstract (e.g., 'up to 94%' figures likely stem from the strongest, least realistic white-box variant).

The detectability/defense discussion (Section 4.6) is comparatively brief and mostly qualitative (a single AUC figure for T2IShield, general remarks about WeightWatcher deviations); no proposed or evaluated concrete mitigation method is offered beyond citing existing detectors, leaving the 'potential remedies' promised in the contributions list underdeveloped.

Some results show non-monotonic or inconsistent trends (e.g., RECE/RECELER sometimes reducing target exposure post-EEB in explicit-content erasure, ESD-X's own baseline high target-recognition rates confounding interpretation in Table 11) that are acknowledged but not fully resolved, slightly complicating the clean narrative of universal EEB success.

The paper relies on a single detector (GCD) for celebrity identification and NudeNet for explicit content as ground truth for ASR; classifier errors/biases could affect the reported numbers, and no human evaluation or cross-validation with a second classifier is reported to corroborate automated metrics.

FLUX experiments (Section 4.5) are limited to only two erasure methods (ESD, UCE) and lack the full breadth (RECE/RECELER/AdvUnlearn, object/explicit-content tasks) applied to SD, so claims of cross-architecture generality are only partially substantiated.
